stances_toward.note: Armenia joined the EAEU in January 2015 and still depends on it (Russia 35.5% of trade, remittances, gas price tied to the 2022 intergovernmental agreement), but resists alignment: the EAEU states' joint statement of May 2026 asked for a referendum on EU membership, Putin says EAEU and EU customs union are incompatible, and on 5 Oct 2026 Pashinyan told the EAEU council that 'no significant progress' had been made in the negotiations while Lukashenko warned against leaving the common market. Pashinyan's line is that the current EU framework (CEPA, without a free-trade part) is compatible. A member that cooperates out of necessity while resisting the political direction of the union.

stances_toward.note: Member of the Eurasian Economic Union and host of the Eurasian Intergovernmental Council in Minsk on 2 Oct 2026, where Lukashenko reaffirmed integration as a priority; the EAEU is the legal frame for about 61% of foreign goods trade with Russia. Partner rather than ally: an economic union, not a defence pact, and Russian measures (SPOT) show members do not set the rules. Bond - affinity.
